Clara / Marissa —

Thanks for the redline and the clear notes. I pulled together quick responses to the four bullets Clara summarized: 

1) Cross-border transfers: We can incorporate the EU SCCs or an explicit EU-US Addendum. We typically include the SCC text by reference and provide the executed addendum via DocuSign. We can accept your preference — please confirm which mechanism Sophos prefers in the redline.

2) Subprocessors: Our standard approach is notice + 30 days to object. For objections grounded in security/regulatory concerns, we require the parties to negotiate in good faith; in practice we also offer an option for customers to request an enhanced data processing addendum for a limited set of critical subprocessors, including scoped audit rights (time-boxed and with reasonable notice).

3) Liability cap: We generally propose symmetrical caps tied to the fees paid in the last 12 months (annual contract value). However, carveouts for gross negligence or willful misconduct remain un-capped. If Sophos insists on removing willful misconduct carveouts, we will need executive approval — please indicate the business rationale.

4) Retention & deletion: Redwood confirms backups are retained for up to X days (we'll provide exact retention in the operational annex) and we perform deletion/de-identification upon contract termination with certification upon request (we'll include a clause to that effect).

On the model-training question: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or content to train models unless there is an explicit, opt-in arrangement. No customer data is used for model improvements by default. We will add an explicit clause in the DPA confirming that.

Next steps: 
- Marissa: can you propose two time slots for a 30–45 minute counsel-to-counsel call? 
- Clara: if you can mark the preferred transfer mechanism in the redline, we will prepare a counter-redline addressing the items above and route for approval.
